references.text: Describes Israel's journey through the great and fearful wilderness, with snakes and scorpions, a dry land without water—the same wilderness experience as in Deuteronomy 32:10
Uses the same expression 'apple of the eye' (כְּאִישׁוֹן עֵינוֹ) as an image of God's protection of his people
The same expression 'apple of the eye' is used to describe God's caring protection
A prayer to be kept as the apple of the eye, using the same image of God's close care
The Lord showed grace to Israel in the wilderness, a people who survived the sword—referring to the same wilderness period
God knew Israel in the wilderness, in the dry land—a parallel to God's care in the wilderness
Describes how God found Israel abandoned and cared for them with love—the same theme of God's care for the helpless people
Whoever touches God's people touches his apple of the eye—using the same image of God's protection
Moses led the people out and performed wonders in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years—referring to the same wilderness period
God carried his people in the wilderness for forty years—the same theme of God's care and protection in the wilderness
